# University of the Andes (Colombia)
Founded in 1948 by Mario Laserna Pinzón, the University of the Andes (Universidad de los Andes) was Colombia’s first nonsectarian and politically neutral university. It was established against a backdrop of political change and economic modernization, emphasizing the need to provide Colombia with technically skilled professionals and liberal education modeled on the American university system. Classes began in 1949 with 80 students, growing rapidly despite political violence in the 1950s, and pioneered programs such as the three/two model allowing students to complete part of their studies abroad.
Legally constituted as a nonprofit in 1948, the university gained formal university status in 1964. It is governed by a Board of Trustees, Board of Directors, and the Rector’s office, with 14 academic units including 10 faculties and various interdisciplinary centers. The university promotes pluralism, academic excellence, and civic responsibility as stated in its Statutes. The campus in Bogotá blends restored religious and industrial buildings with modern facilities including extensive classrooms, laboratories, and libraries. Its student body is highly selective, with 95% of undergraduates coming from the top 1% of high school graduates nationally, and it offers extensive international exchange programs through partnerships with over 119 universities worldwide. The institution is symbolized by its mascot, Seneca the goat, and counts among its notable alumni numerous Colombian political leaders, ministers, academics, artists, and professionals.
